newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU 1997/98 grain exports seen at 27-30 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: EU 1997/98 grain exports seen at 27-30 mln tonnes.

text.p: European Union grain exports may range between 27 and 30 million tonnes in the 1997/98 season after 27 million in 1996/97, grain trader Alfred Toepfer's latest newsletter said on Friday.

The level of exports would depend on how successfully EU exporters competed in markets such as North Africa where not only the United States, but Romania, Hungary and the Ukraine were also likely to appear, it said.
Toepfer said eastern Europe should have an exportable surplus of 15 million tonnes in 1997/98.
Toepfer pegged the EU's 1997 grain harvest at 196-199 million tonnes, down from 200 million last year.
This compares with the present estimates in a range of 195-205 million for 1997 projected by traders, analysts and the EU commission.

While the area was expanded by two percent to 37.2 million hectares and crops were looking good in northern Europe, yields had fallen in northern France and Mediterranean countries as a result of a spring drought and heavy rainfall of late, it said.
EU grain consumption in 1997/98 was seen broadly steady at 172.7 million tonnes of which feed use might be a steady 108 million.
Cheap corngluten and soymeal were expected to compete with feed grain in compound feed and regain some lost market share.
The potential 1997/98 exports would be within limits set for the EU's subsidised allocation in world trade agreements allowing 28.1 million tonnes plus 1.5-2.0 million of food aid.
The total included 16.85 million wheat (including flour and semolina) as well as 11.3 million tonnes of feed grain (including malt).
Toepfer said the EU should be more aggressive in its wheat export policy, by for example offering five to 10 ecus per tonne to be able to compete with the U.S. in North Africa.
Harvests worldwide were looking favourable and prices were pointing lower and the EU needed to be more generous if it wanted to get rid of the available grain volumes.
